title: Phantom Blade Zero Best Build - What A Build Actually Consists Of
description: There is no published tier list for Phantom Blade Zero, and nobody has measured the weapons yet. What is verified: a build is two main weapons, two Phantom Edges, two flasks and six accessories, upgraded with Remnant Dust, and bosses are the source.

sections.title: The Honest Answer About A Best Build
sections.content:
No tier list exists. The game is reviewed but not yet played by the public, and no outlet has published per-weapon measurements, so any "best build" table written today is a guess with formatting. What can be stated is what a build is made of, and that is more useful than a ranking: this game has no character levels, so the build is the kit.

The slot layout, from the community combat write-up this site has cross-checked: two main weapons, two Phantom Edges, two flasks and six accessories. Weapons can be swapped mid-combat, which is a defensive tool as well as an offensive one - see combat.

sections.title: The Five Things That Make Up A Build
sections.content:
1. A main weapon pair. 30-plus exist, grouped one-handed, two-handed and dual-wielded, each with its own attack, guard-break value, special and execution. Length and speed trade against each other - see weapons for the named roster.
  2. Two Phantom Edges. 20-plus, consumed from a separate resource that kills feed back into, and several double as traversal keys - the reason skipping an area can lock a build option, see collectibles.
  3. Two flasks. Different flasks restore health, raise attack or speed up refined Sha-chi gain; some change your move set.
  4. Six accessories. Pure passives, and the pre-order Treasure Basin is one (reported to raise Remnant Dust drop rate by 10%) - see pre-order guide.
  5. Weapon upgrades. Material-driven, capped at 30 levels, unlocking new moves rather than bigger numbers, and resettable with no loss - so a build is a commitment for a session, not for the save file.

sections.title: Where The Parts Come From
sections.content: From bosses and from the map. S-GAME states that defeating powerful foes yields their weapons and their signature techniques, and the director has said the boss count and the weapon count track each other - which is why the boss list is the closest thing this site has to a build roadmap. No per-boss drop has been published, so none is claimed here.

sections.title: What The Reviews Say About Building
sections.content:
• Variety is a headline strength. SteamDeckHQ (100) credits "the variety of weapons and their abilities"; Areajugones (95) says the arsenal "gives every weapon real personality"; Saudi Gamer (100) a "huge selection of weapons"; Gameliner (90) "incredibly smooth, varied" combat.
  • No grinding path. GAMES.CH (85) calls the reduced reliance on repetitive farming a differentiator from traditional soulslikes - consistent with there being no XP system.
  • But crowds are flat. GameSpot (8/10) found mowing down weak enemies tiring, so a group-clear weapon and a boss weapon are different questions.
  • 50 to 55 hours of it, per IGN and Combo Infinito - see how long to beat.

What this page will become at launch: per-weapon notes filled from player measurement rather than speculation, with the source of each claim recorded.

sections.title: Why This Page Exists Now
sections.content: Search Console had been serving three impressions of this URL at an average position of 4.0 while no such page existed - a phantom entry inherited from how the site was linked, and a wasted ranking. The page now exists so that position has something to point at, and it deliberately publishes structure instead of a fake ranking. If you came here looking for a tier list: it does not exist yet, and this page says so rather than inventing one.
